summary: Fires anywhere in the lower 48 can now be prepared, and NWS / local officials' alerts are national. M1 weather quota: Open-Meteo limit answers are never retried or cached, there is a per-host block until the reset, `weather-probe`, `build --require-hrrr`, and a refused refresh keeps the old weather with a plain warning. M2 build anywhere: the build gate uses catalog.resolve_listed + is_supported (404/409/422 texts as the API), LANDFIRE editions LF2023/LF2024/LF2025 with an older-only NoData switch and an 'unknown, not low' outside-coverage label, perimeters matched by IRWIN id (California path proven unchanged on recorded answers), fire-local time everywhere in build/spread (no Pacific default), the issuer's own name in every record-derived text, and the interim live fuel moisture warning outside California. M3 national NWS: one request for the 49 areas, local officials' messages (NWEM) from the NWS API, and an OpenFEMA IPAWS archive channel for past dates. Cut-line items (a) OpenFEMA prefetch, (b) weighted counter + soft cap + hourly refetch and (d) growth_sorensen are done; (c) used its fallback test (no active Southern/Eastern fire of 1,000 ac or more). M4: Horse Gulch (MT) built with HRRR only and passes check_bundle with 0 problems; Black Cove (NC) is pending (quota): the Open-Meteo historical-forecast daily limit was reached at 02:04Z and resets at 2026-10-24T00:00Z, 22 h away, so under the stop rule it was not waited for.

contract_deviations: §14.12.2 probe_open_meteo returns an extra `detail` key; every request-limit period (daily, hourly, per-minute) is reported as status `daily_limit`, with the period named in `detail`.

§14.12.2 'no retries': a per-minute Open-Meteo refusal is waited out once inside om_request (next minute + 1 s, at most 65 s), because other tenants of the shared IP pushed the archive host over its 600-a-minute limit and a whole build failing on a one-minute limit wastes every other request. Daily and hourly refusals are never retried.

§14.7 OpenFEMA: the server-side $filter is by date window and status only (event and area filters are applied locally after parsing), windows are bounded to 22 days, and `references` come from a second query (originalMessage) for non-Alert messages only.
§14.7 a county match has `covers_reported_location` and `nearest_km` null (only polygon matches fill them), so a county-wide message is never presented as covering the fire's point.
§14.7 `polygon` may be a GeoJSON MultiPolygon when an archived message had several areas.
§14.7 the archive channel waits up to openfema.REQUEST_WAIT_S = 3 s before answering `pending` (a catalog lookup of an unbuilt fire can add about 2 s).
observed.SOURCE_PREFIXES is now ('NASA FIRMS', 'NIFC WFIGS fire perimeters', 'NASA CMR') so the observed step no longer removes the pipeline's 'NIFC WFIGS incident record (IRWIN)' data source.

§14.12.2 (review round 1, R3): a daily Open-Meteo block is re-checked with one tiny probe request at most once an hour and lifted when the host answers (the contract says no network call until 00:00 UTC). A contract decision for the integration.
§14.7 (review round 1, R2): API build jobs only start the OpenFEMA background fetch; CLI builds fetch synchronously, at most 15 s per request with no retry.

R2.detail: API build jobs no longer wait for FEMA. api.jobs runs every job inside pipeline.background_followups(); there pipeline.archive_prefetch only starts the one deduplicated background fetch (openfema.start) and returns, so a 'Prepare analysis' job ends when its bundle is ready (CONTRACT 14.7 'a successful build also starts it'). JobManager.drain also waits for those follow-up threads (so tests never leave a fetch running after their offline guard is gone). A CLI build (its process would kill a daemon thread) still fetches synchronously, each request capped at openfema.PREFETCH_TIMEOUT_S = 15 s with no retry. openfema.prefetch now returns 'stored' / 'started' / 'skipped' / 'failed' and does not restart a window that failed less than 10 min ago. Documented under Deviations.

R3.outcome: fixed (a deviation from CONTRACT 14.12.2 as written; the integration should fold it into the contract)
R3.detail: A daily block is re-checked by weather.recheck_daily_block(label) with one tiny uncached probe request (the probe's own parameters, retries=0) at most once an hour (DAILY_RECHECK_S = 3600, counted from the block or the last re-check; the re-check time is claimed under the lock, so concurrent callers make one request). An answer lifts the block and the request goes ahead; a limit answer renews it; anything else keeps it. Used by om_request and raise_if_blocked (the build preflight). Hourly and per-minute blocks are unchanged. Cost: at most 24 tiny requests a day per blocked host. This round's own probes show why: the refused host changed every 10-20 minutes.

R4.detail: The LEW record in tests/data/official/openfema_window_frw.json keeps only its event code: its WEA texts (CMAMtext, CMAMlongtext; its description is empty and it has no headline or instruction, so the reviewer's ':3375 description' was the CMAMlongtext) are 'Text removed by hand: a Law Enforcement Warning kept only for its event code (scope-filter test).' PROVENANCE.md says so under 'Set by hand'; the recorder applies the same rule (TEXT_REMOVED_CODES) and its check fails if an LEW text survives. The sample's wording-scan hits ('safe location', 'official all-clear') went with the text.
